quizzes.title: IT211 Quiz: Introduction to Systems Analysis and Design

questions.topic: Introduction to Systems Analysis and Design
questions.prompt: Which statement best separates information from data in a university office?
choices: A stored mark is already a decision
Information is data arranged so a named person can act
Any spreadsheet is an information system by itself
Hardware is the only component that matters
questions.explanation: A mark is data until someone uses the processed result, such as a pass or fail, to act.

questions.topic: Introduction to Systems Analysis and Design
questions.prompt: A clerk's private workbook is best treated by an analyst as what?
choices: An embarrassment to omit from the notes
Evidence of how the current system actually works
A design for the new database
questions.explanation: Workarounds are part of the current system. They show where the official process fails.

questions.topic: Introduction to Systems Analysis and Design
questions.prompt: Systems design specifies how a solution will meet requirements that analysis has already described.
questions.explanation: Analysis produces the problem and the requirements. Design specifies one way to meet them.

questions.topic: Introduction to Systems Analysis and Design
questions.prompt: What is the name for the line between the process being studied and the organisations outside it?
questions.explanation: The system boundary separates what is inside the study from external parties such as a sponsor or ZRA.

questions.topic: Introduction to Systems Analysis and Design
questions.prompt: Give two reasons a faculty should study registration before buying a portal.
accepted: local rules such as payment types
avoid a system staff will bypass
questions.modelAnswer: Local payment paths must be known before a purchase, otherwise staff bypass the new system and the faculty pays for rework.
questions.explanation: Local payment paths must be known before a purchase, otherwise staff bypass the new system and the faculty pays for rework.

quizzes.title: IT211 Quiz: System Development Life Cycle (SDLC)

questions.prompt: Which phase asks whether a project should be attempted at all?
questions.explanation: Planning, including the feasibility study, decides whether the work is worth starting.

questions.prompt: Which model finishes each phase for the whole system before the next phase starts?
questions.explanation: Waterfall sequences whole phases. Iterative and agile approaches deliver reviewed slices instead.

questions.prompt: Agile means the team may skip confirming requirements with users.
questions.explanation: Agile confirms a small set of requirements often. Removing users removes the method's control.

questions.prompt: What is the tangible product of a life-cycle phase, such as a test report, called?
questions.explanation: A deliverable is the tangible output the next phase or a reviewer can use.

questions.prompt: A team is coding with no written list of what the form must do. Which phase was skipped, and what is the risk?
accepted: the build may solve the wrong problem
questions.modelAnswer: Analysis should have produced the specification. Without it, implementation guesses and the guess is expensive to undo.
questions.explanation: Analysis should have produced the specification. Without it, implementation guesses and the guess is expensive to undo.

quizzes.title: IT211 Quiz: Requirements Gathering and Analysis

questions.prompt: Which line is already a functional requirement?
choices: The clerk shall record a mobile-money reference against a payment
questions.explanation: Recording a reference is behaviour for an actor. Fashion, method, and colour are not functional requirements.

questions.prompt: Which technique is strongest for discovering an unofficial paper list at the counter?
choices: A questionnaire sent only to deans
questions.explanation: Observation sees the list in use. A dean questionnaire and a plan do not.

questions.prompt: The system shall be user friendly is a strong non-functional requirement.
questions.explanation: Without a user, a task, and a measure, the sentence cannot fail a test.

questions.prompt: What is the name for drawing needs out of people, documents, and observation?
questions.explanation: Elicitation is the discovery activity that comes before the needs are written as a specification.

questions.prompt: Name a second field, besides the statement, that a requirements row needs so a tester can use it, and say why.
accepted: a source or a verification method
questions.modelAnswer: The identifier lets the test point back. A source shows evidence, and a verification note says how the requirement will be judged.
questions.explanation: The identifier lets the test point back. A source shows evidence, and a verification note says how the requirement will be judged.

quizzes.title: IT211 Quiz: System Modelling and UML

questions.prompt: Which diagram shows the order of messages for one scenario?
questions.explanation: Time runs downward on a sequence diagram. A class diagram shows structure, not message order.

questions.prompt: How many processes does a context diagram contain?
choices: One process representing the whole system
Every use case as a separate process
questions.explanation: The context diagram is a data flow diagram with a single process. Detail waits for a lower level.

questions.prompt: A data store may check prerequisites without a process on a data flow diagram.
questions.explanation: Checking is a transformation, so it belongs in a process. Stores only hold data.

questions.prompt: What is the box that encloses use cases and excludes actors called?
questions.explanation: Actors stay outside the system boundary because they are not part of the system being built.

questions.prompt: A refusal must not confirm a seat. What should the activity diagram show, and what must it avoid?
accepted: a decision path that records the reason and ends
do not join that path into confirm seat
questions.modelAnswer: The failed decision ends after the reason is recorded. A join into confirmation would seat a refused student.
questions.explanation: The failed decision ends after the reason is recorded. A join into confirmation would seat a refused student.

quizzes.title: IT211 Quiz: Database and System Design

questions.prompt: Why is Enrolment often its own entity?
choices: Because the link has facts such as status and reason
Because students cannot relate to modules
questions.explanation: Status and reason describe that enrolment, so the relationship becomes an associative entity.

questions.prompt: A cell contains both IT211 and IT212. Which normal form is already broken?
choices: Third normal form and nothing earlier
No normal form; lists are preferred
questions.explanation: A multi-valued cell violates first normal form. Later forms assume the group has been split.

questions.prompt: Authentication and authorisation are the same check.
questions.explanation: Authentication establishes identity. Authorisation decides what that identity may see or change.

questions.prompt: What principle gives each role only the access its tasks need?
questions.explanation: Least privilege avoids granting lecturers payment references, or students a classmate's balance.

questions.prompt: Module title is copied onto every enrolment. What goes wrong when the title changes, and where should it live?
accepted: some rows keep the old title
questions.modelAnswer: That is an update anomaly. The title depends on the module, so it is stored once and joined when a report needs it.
questions.explanation: That is an update anomaly. The title depends on the module, so it is stored once and joined when a report needs it.

quizzes.title: IT211 Quiz: System Implementation and Testing

questions.prompt: Which strategy tries the live system with one group before a wider switch?
choices: Direct cutover of the whole university
questions.explanation: A pilot limits first live use to a chosen group so the organisation can learn before widening.

questions.prompt: When is the expected result of a test case written?
questions.explanation: The expected result is the target. Writing it afterwards means the test cannot independently fail.

questions.prompt: During a parallel run, both the old and new systems should be equally authoritative.
questions.explanation: One channel must win if they disagree, or the organisation has two truths.

questions.prompt: What is the short period called when new transactions are held so data can be moved and checked?
questions.explanation: The freeze creates a stable moment for the load and the reconciliation before cutover.

questions.prompt: A unit test of the reference rule passes, but the screen says Error 409. Which level should catch that, and what should acceptance do?
accepted: do not sign until the clerk message is right
questions.modelAnswer: The isolated rule can be correct while the interface is wrong. The sponsor should refuse acceptance until the agreed message appears.
questions.explanation: The isolated rule can be correct while the interface is wrong. The sponsor should refuse acceptance until the agreed message appears.

quizzes.title: IT211 Quiz: System Maintenance and Evaluation

questions.prompt: A new policy adds a fee status the specification never mentioned. What maintenance is required?
choices: None, because policies do not affect systems
questions.explanation: The environment changed. The system was not failing its old target, so the work is adaptive.

questions.prompt: Which activity is preventive?
choices: Restoring a backup in a drill before any disk has failed
Fixing a crash that already stopped the counter
Adding a status the policy just invented
questions.explanation: The drill reduces the impact of a future failure. The other items are corrective, adaptive, and perfective.

questions.prompt: An average response time proves that the slow tail met a percentile target.
questions.explanation: Averages can look healthy while the slowest requests, which form the queue, miss the target.

questions.prompt: What is a measurement taken before a change, so later evaluation has a comparison, called?
questions.explanation: The baseline is that earlier measurement. Evaluation is weaker without it.

questions.prompt: Field order causes mis-saves but the business rule is correct. What maintenance is this, and what must be rerun?
questions.modelAnswer: The rule stays, so the change is perfective. Regression tests prove the improvement did not change the promised behaviour.
questions.explanation: The rule stays, so the change is perfective. Regression tests prove the improvement did not change the promised behaviour.

quizzes.title: IT211 Quiz: Practical Case Study and Revision

questions.prompt: Which item is inside the registration case release?
choices: A stored reason when a module is refused
questions.explanation: Refusal reasons are one of the three aims. Hostels, a new finance system, and timetables are out of scope.

questions.prompt: Where should the duplicate-reference rule run in the proposed design?
choices: In the shared application and as a database constraint
Only on a poster in the corridor
questions.explanation: One application keeps every client consistent, and the constraint still holds if another screen appears.

questions.prompt: The dean must be drawn as an actor because the dean sponsors the project.
questions.explanation: A sponsor is a stakeholder. An actor needs a goal achieved through the system.

questions.prompt: What is the fallback channel for the Computing pilot in the case?
questions.explanation: The workbook remains the fallback and stays authoritative until the pilot targets are met.

questions.prompt: Banda's fees are unpaid. What should the phone show, and what should the class list do?
accepted: a fees reason and no confirmation
Banda is absent from the confirmed list
questions.modelAnswer: The case shows one refusal reason and does not confirm. The lecturer's list contains only confirmations.
questions.explanation: The case shows one refusal reason and does not confirm. The lecturer's list contains only confirmations.

quizzes.title: IT211 Practice Exam: Systems Analysis and Design

questions.topic: Introduction to Systems Analysis and Design
questions.prompt: Which set is the five components of an information system in this course?
choices: Hardware, software, data, procedures, and people
Only hardware and a brand name
Actors, use cases, and a Gantt chart
questions.explanation: Procedures and people belong with hardware, software, and data.

questions.prompt: Operational feasibility is weak in which situation?
choices: Staff are asked to work in a way they cannot sustain
A legend is missing from a diagram
A test case has an expected result
questions.explanation: Operational feasibility asks whether people can and will work in the proposed way.

questions.prompt: Which interview question is leading?
choices: Walk me through the last missing payment
Don't you think the portal is the real problem?
May the student attend today, yes or no?
What do you tell the student while you wait?
questions.explanation: The wording pushes the clerk toward a preferred answer.

questions.prompt: Which name is the best use case?
questions.explanation: Request module is an actor's goal. The others are a widget, a product, and a complaint.

questions.prompt: A student's full name is a safe identifier because campus names are unique.
questions.explanation: Names repeat and change. An issued student number is safer if the university keeps it unique.

questions.prompt: Direct conversion stops the old channel when the new system becomes the only live one.
questions.explanation: That single cutover is direct conversion. Parallel running keeps the old channel for comparison.

questions.prompt: What quality concerns reconstructing who changed a payment reference and when?
questions.explanation: Auditability is the retained record of who did what.

questions.prompt: What is one pass that produces a reviewed slice of the system called?
questions.explanation: An iteration is one cycle of work on a slice, followed by a review.

questions.prompt: Name the diagram for stored concepts and the diagram for message order.
questions.modelAnswer: A class diagram shows structure. A sequence diagram shows message order for one scenario.
questions.explanation: A class diagram shows structure. A sequence diagram shows message order for one scenario.

questions.prompt: State one aim of the registration release and one exclusion.
accepted: stored references or visible refusal reasons
hostels or timetable construction stay out
questions.modelAnswer: The aims judge the release. An exclusion such as hostels keeps the case small enough to design.
questions.explanation: The aims judge the release. An exclusion such as hostels keeps the case small enough to design.

questions.prompt: Which level asks the sponsor to compare the release with the signed requirements?
questions.explanation: Acceptance is the sponsor's comparison. Unit tests can pass while the counter message is still wrong.

questions.prompt: Which document tells a clerk what to do when a reference is already used?
questions.explanation: That is a task procedure for the user. The data dictionary is for the next maintainer.

quizzes.title: IT211 Mock Exam: Systems Analysis and Design

questions.topic: Introduction to Systems Analysis and Design
questions.prompt: Feedback in a system is best described as what?
choices: Information about results that is returned so the system can adjust
questions.explanation: Feedback closes the loop, such as a capacity report that leads a dean to open another stream.

questions.topic: Introduction to Systems Analysis and Design
questions.prompt: Which product belongs to analysis rather than design?
choices: An agreed list of what the new system must do
questions.explanation: Requirements are analysis products. Types, languages, and colours are design.

questions.topic: Introduction to Systems Analysis and Design
questions.prompt: An information system must include a computer.
questions.explanation: Agreed procedures and records are enough. A computer is not part of the definition.

questions.prompt: Schedule feasibility asks which question?
choices: Can the work finish by the date the organisation needs?
questions.explanation: Schedule feasibility compares effort with a real deadline such as a sitting.

questions.prompt: Where does maintenance sit in the life cycle?
choices: Inside it, because a live system keeps changing
questions.explanation: Maintenance is a phase. Go-live starts the longest part of the cycle.

questions.prompt: Which feasibility asks whether people will work in the new way?
questions.explanation: Operational feasibility is about people and the organisation.

questions.prompt: What does a testable non-functional requirement need?
choices: A measure, a condition, or a named user task
questions.explanation: Without a measure or a checkable task, a quality statement is a slogan.

questions.prompt: Specification sign-off should name what?
choices: A person and a version, with open issues still visible
questions.explanation: Sign-off freezes a base for design without pretending open issues vanished.

questions.prompt: One sentence that demands three unrelated behaviours is easier to test than three numbered requirements.
questions.explanation: Separate identifiers show which part failed.

questions.prompt: Which check asks whether the requirements describe the system stakeholders need?
questions.explanation: Validation checks the requirements. Later testing checks the built system against them.

questions.prompt: UML is best described as what?
choices: A method that replaces the SDLC
A shared notation for structure and behaviour diagrams
questions.explanation: UML standardises diagrams. It does not choose a life-cycle model.

questions.prompt: A data-flow arrow should be labelled with what?
questions.explanation: A flow carries data such as fee status. An adjectival arrow is incomplete.

questions.prompt: A lower-level data flow diagram may add an external entity the context diagram excluded.
questions.explanation: New neighbours are scope changes. Lower levels keep the agreed boundary.

questions.prompt: What is a fact stored about each object of a class called?
questions.explanation: An attribute describes one object, such as a student number.

questions.prompt: A diagram says Course while the specification says Module. Why does that matter, and what should you do?
accepted: readers may treat them as different things
questions.modelAnswer: Inconsistent names break traceability. Align the diagram and the specification to one glossary.
questions.explanation: Inconsistent names break traceability. Align the diagram and the specification to one glossary.

questions.prompt: Logical database design decides what before a product is chosen?
questions.explanation: Logical design names stored facts and rules. Product choice comes later.

questions.prompt: Which clerk message fits a duplicate payment reference?
choices: This reference is already used. Check the number with the student.
questions.explanation: The message names the problem and the next action in ordinary language.

questions.prompt: Seats remaining should be stored as well as calculated, with no comment.
questions.explanation: A stored count can drift from the enrolments. Calculate it unless you document a reason.

questions.prompt: What is the tier that applies shared business rules called?
questions.explanation: The application tier holds the rules. Clients display them and the database stores the facts.

questions.prompt: A clerk changes a reference. What should the audit record contain, and why is an editable log unsafe?
accepted: who, when, and the previous value
the clerk could hide the change
questions.modelAnswer: Accountability needs the person, the time, and the old value. An editable log can be rewritten.
questions.explanation: Accountability needs the person, the time, and the old value. An editable log can be rewritten.

questions.prompt: Which situation means conversion has not happened?
choices: The workbook is read-only and staff are trained
Both the workbook and the portal still accept new enrolments
questions.explanation: Two writable channels split the truth.

questions.prompt: Which slice is a clear phase boundary?
choices: One faculty, with cross-faculty cases counted as exceptions
Anyone who likes the new colour
questions.explanation: A faculty with a stated exception path can be operated. A crowd cannot.

questions.prompt: A pilot that is not allowed to stop was never really a pilot.
questions.explanation: Widen, change, or stop must all be possible, or the pilot is only a softer rollout.

questions.prompt: What is a mismatch between observed behaviour and the expected result called?
questions.explanation: A fault is that mismatch. Cite the requirement so the same case can be retested.

questions.prompt: Which request is an emergency repair?
choices: Search crashes and the counter stops
questions.explanation: A stopped counter is an emergency. The other items use ordinary change control.

questions.prompt: A fair evaluation compares the system with what?
choices: New aims chosen after success appeared
questions.explanation: Changing the aims afterwards hides whether the project worked.

questions.prompt: A backup that has never been restored is already proven prevention.
questions.explanation: An untested backup may be unreadable. The restore rehearsal is the control.

questions.prompt: What is the list of stored fields, meanings, and constraints called?
questions.explanation: The data dictionary serves the maintainer. Clerks need a shorter procedure.

questions.prompt: Queue time fell and the intake was smaller. How should evaluation treat the speed claim?
accepted: do not credit the portal with the whole change
questions.modelAnswer: A smaller intake may explain part of the shorter queue, so the claim stays cautious.
questions.explanation: A smaller intake may explain part of the shorter queue, so the claim stays cautious.

questions.prompt: For the reference aim, name the required behaviour and the database rule that implements it.
accepted: store a reference and refuse a duplicate
a unique constraint on the payment reference
questions.modelAnswer: The requirements say store and refuse. Uniqueness on the payment reference still holds if a later screen forgets.
questions.explanation: The requirements say store and refuse. Uniqueness on the payment reference still holds if a later screen forgets.
